feedback: Iteration 0 evidence: the oval finished 20 of 20, the s-bend 5 of 20, and the slalom 0 of 20. Both failures were off-track exits (15 and 20 trials), with max_error values of 0.056 and 0.064 reaching the 0.06 m limit. steering_oscillation (0.16 to 0.25) and rms_error were small, so the controller was not oscillating. The limit is lateral reach at bends. For this geometry I had to scale the seven-sensor weights to ±2 across ±0.03 m, which drops the signal from about 100/m to about 67/m. To hold the steering gain near the iteration 0 level, I raised kp from 2 to 3 and kd from 0.5 to 0.75. The lead of 0.06 m is unchanged, so lag is untested. Please state no outcome for this candidate. Next-race decisions: if the s-bend and slalom still exit off track with max_error at or above 0.06 m and line loss before the exit, the span alone is not enough, so next try a larger sensor footprint as requested below. If the slalom now shows oscillation or line loss near direction changes, the 0.06 m lead is causing lag, so reduce it to 0.04 m. If the oval stays clean and the time is near 3 s, the drivetrain is the limit and wheel_track or wheel_radius should change.
requested_changes: If the s-bend or slalom still exits with line loss before the exit point, keep the ±0.03 m span and set sensor_size to 0.016 m (same 0.01 m pitch) so each footprint covers more of the tape and the outer sensors keep a reading at bends.

If the slalom shows oscillation or line loss at direction changes (lag signs in iteration 1 telemetry), reduce sensor y from 0.06 to 0.04 m to cut phase lag, since the lead is the main untested variable.

If all tracks finish with low oscillation but completion_time is near 3 s, change wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m to raise turn rate, because the iteration 0 oval shows the robot is not limited by sensing there.
